story_text.value:
I've been building Fusor. It's a reactive web framework for Rust where the templates are plain HTML files, so there's no markup living inside Rust macros like view! or rsx!.

The state and logic live in ordinary Rust structs, and the whole app compiles to WASM. It also benefits from Rust type checkers, even for the HTML bindings.

The Fusor website is fully built using the framework. It's all experimental, so I expect breaking changes and lots of refactors.

Any feedback is welcome, and so are contributions! The project is pro AI, if you do decide to contribute.

title.value: Show HN: Fusor – Like Vue, but the logic is Rust

story_text.value:
I'm an American who got married to a Mauritian this past May. We had our Hindu wedding in my wife's home country of Mauritius. My family and friends are not Hindu, and certainly had never been to the tiny island of Mauritius (it's off the coast of Madagascar in case you were wondering).

My wife and I arrived in Mauritius only two weeks before the start of the wedding to put the final preparations in place. I dreaded the prospect of answering a billion questions from my guests while trying to do this. I also dreaded them not having a way to find the answers.

So I made an AI app that acted as a guest concierge. At first I simply made a wedding db, seeded it with our info, connected an MCP server with tools to it, connected the agent to it, and gave all my guests an invite link to use it.

Scope creep took over and now I have an entire AI platform for planning weddings and being a guest concierge. The two sides are actually really complementary to each other: to make the ai answer correctly, you need a knowledge base. So the wedding planning aspect just kind of happened as a result.

There's so much more to this and I'm more than happy to discuss everything I've learned -- for example, the number one thing my guests did with the ai on the day of the ceremony was try to jailbreak it.

The demo I'm sharing here is an example wedding where you get to act as a guest and can interact with the ai concierge. I hope you find it interesting!

title.value: Show HN: An AI wedding concierge I built and ran at my own 300-person wedding

story_text.value:
It improves the usual workflow: take a screenshot, switch to a chat tab, upload it, switch back. - Built with Rust and Tauri v2, including a built-in native screenshot solution for maximum performance and stability. - Answers come from OpenAI models. Fast, the default, usually starts answering within 1–2 seconds; Best is slightly slower, but provides a much higher quality response. - Free is 3 captures a day, up to 10 a week, on Fast, and needs an email sign-in, since usage is metered per account. Plus is $10/month: 2,500 credits a month, the Best model (25 credits per answer, follow-ups included; Fast is 1), and up to 10 follow-ups per capture instead of 2. - Windows 10/11, and Linux on Wayland (GNOME 45+ or KDE Plasma 6). No macOS yet, and no X11.

What I'd most like to know: 1. Is this workflow actually quicker than what you do now? 2. Squint Plus is currently $10/month or $99/year: a) At what monthly price would Plus feel like a good deal? b) At what price would it start to feel expensive, though you'd still consider it? c) At what price would it be too expensive to consider at all? 3. Did anything break during install, sign-in, or a capture?

Thanks!

title.value: Show HN: Squint – Drag a box on your screen and ask AI about it

i kept collecting rare internal company docs + out-of-print business books in random folders, so i put them all on one page.

bottom shelf has hard-to-find books from the founders/leaders of ibm, hp, gm, fastenal and others.

everything links to a free legal source. original pdf/scan when i could find one, otherwise internet archive.

story_text.value:
I’m building Orglet, a desktop app where you give AI workers (I call them orglets, and they are cute) their own instructions and talk to them individually or together in a group chat.

You can build your own army of orglets using your existing Claude Code or Codex subscription, an API provider, or even locally hosted models.

Like other agent harnesses, orglets can access a working folder you give them permission to use. They can split the work among themselves, and you can review the resulting diff before applying changes to your files. Each orglet has its own role, tools and permissions.

Orglet is free under AGPLv3. Downloads are available for Windows, macOS and Linux. It is still very early and flaky, so I’d appreciate any contributions. Thank you!

story_text.value:
I built EthosLM to turn a description of a place into something you can walk around in Minecraft.

The demo starts with “Build me Ba Sing Se.” It produces a city with districts, roads, walls and furnished interiors. Here's the one-minute video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lgixrYLWfhc

It works by separating planning from construction. The model chooses the layout and style. A deterministic library generates the buildings, places the blocks and checks the result.

Buildings use reusable procedural generators rather than completed schematics. The same system can build a wide variety of things from villages to castles in any terrain.

title.value: Show HN: EthosLM - Turn a sentence into a Minecraft city

story_text.value:
Hi HN,

here, what started as a small personal tool, I wanted to create an AI agent-friendly way to fetch and store financial data, like bank accounts, their respective balances and transactions and store them in a small SQLite database, to gather all of them in a single place, store them long term, and assign arbitrary metadata, for example, expense categories, etc.

There are not many PSD2 compliant providers, that allow access to personal bank accounts, but Enable Banking is one of the rare few. That is why it is the core of the engine used to access the financial data from different ASPSPs.

Thus, it is quite easy to register and set up a personal "application" and link your existing bank accounts to access them in the banker CLI.

I hope you find it useful!

title.value: Show HN: Banker – CLI for your finances using Enable Banking and SQLite
